features.source: Huronia, the country between Nottawasaga Bay and Lake Simcoe that the four (later five) Wendat nations — the Huron of the French records — held as one confederacy from about the middle of the fifteenth century. It is drawn at the compact settled extent — some two dozen palisaded towns in a district a few days' walk across, not the far wider reach of its trade — and ends with the Haudenosaunee campaigns of 1649 and the burning of Sainte-Marie in 1650, after which the survivors dispersed and the confederacy no longer held ground.
